extracted.intended_audience: FCC program participants, program administrators, and suspension/debarment officials (SDOs); legal practitioners advising covered parties
extracted.subtask_description: Rules and evaluative standards the FCC adopts to implement OMB suspension and debarment Guidelines for its covered programs (e.g., Lifeline, E-Rate, RHC, TRS, NDBEDP), including causes, factors, evidentiary standards, exceptions, and transition/continuation policies. Guidance is aimed at SDOs deciding whether to initiate suspensions/debarments and at participants on how conduct will be assessed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adoption of OMB Guidelines' causes and factors
rubrics_metrics.description: The Commission adopts the causes for exclusion articulated in the OMB Guidelines (2 CFR 180.800) and the aggravating and mitigating factors (2 CFR 180.860), and supplements them with FCC-specific examples and factors in Supplemental Rule 6001.450.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adopting the Guidelines provides flexibility to the Commission while giving program participants notice. Supplemental Rule 6001.450(a) aligns with the Guidelines' causes; subsections (b) and (c) align with factors. The FCC builds on longstanding history and widespread adoption of the Guidelines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Two-category structure for causes
rubrics_metrics.description: Causes for suspension or debarment fall into two categories: (i) violations of program-specific rules that affect program integrity; and (ii) violations of other applicable Commission rules that affect present responsibility.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The first group is focused on conduct undermining specific program integrity (e.g., false forms leading to overpayments). The second group addresses broader conduct relevant to present responsibility (e.g., single serious rule violation or repeated violations, habitual non-payment of regulatory fees).

rubrics_metrics.name: Program-specific integrity violations (examples)
rubrics_metrics.description: Violation[s] of the terms of a public agreement or transaction, specific to FCC programs, that could be so serious as to affect the integrity of those programs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes but is not limited to: willful or grossly negligent submission of false or misleading FCC forms or statements or other documentation that result in or could result in overpayments; willful or grossly negligent violation of statutory/regulatory provisions applicable to Covered Programs; and willful, grossly negligent, or habitual failure to respond to Commission or administrator requests for information to justify payment or continued certification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consideration of failure to respond and recordkeeping
rubrics_metrics.description: When evaluating failure to respond to information requests, the SDO will consider compliance with document retention regulations and the quality and credibility of evidence presented.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Not all failures to respond will be serious enough to affect program integrity; SDOs must evaluate the facts and circumstances, including documentation quality and retention compliance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Commission-rule violations affecting present responsibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Causes include (1) a single serious violation of Commission rules or repeated violations of Commission rules; or (2) a single substantial or habitual non-payment or under-payment of Commission regulatory fees.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A single serious violation is one that materially and negatively affects the participant's present responsibility. Habitual nonpayment can be treated as repeated rule violations and assessed case-by-case.

rubrics_metrics.name: No automatic or dispositive triggers for exclusion
rubrics_metrics.description: Identification of causes is not the same as creating automatic triggers that always require exclusion; a finding that a 'cause' exists does not automatically result in suspension or debarment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: SDOs must evaluate conduct based on causes plus aggravating and mitigating factors and the unique circumstances of each case. The process is forward-looking and fact-specific rather than rigidly formulaic.

rubrics_metrics.name: Case-by-case determination and flexibility
rubrics_metrics.description: SDOs must consider the unique circumstances of each case, including whether a cause is 'so serious or compelling' that it affects present responsibility.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This mirrors approaches in other contexts (e.g., licensing). The Guidelines' flexibility is intentionally preserved; SDOs may consider mitigating circumstances even where some rules impose strict liability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Willfulness standard (ordinary meaning and limits)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Guidelines do not define 'willful'; courts suggest it generally applies to knowing or reckless violations rather than mere negligence. For purposes of both section 180.800 and the supplemental rule, 'willful' will not ordinarily include minor, isolated, and inadvertent noncompliance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Commission precedent sometimes interprets 'willful' expansively, but the supplemental rule adopts a pragmatic approach that excludes routine inadvertent errors from 'willful' in ordinary cases. However, the Guidelines permit debarment for any cause 'so serious or compelling' even absent willfulness.

rubrics_metrics.name: History of failures as basis for debarment
rubrics_metrics.description: A history of failure to perform or unsatisfactory performance of a public transaction may support debarment if it is so serious as to affect the integrity of a Federal agency program.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Multiple minor violations across projects can aggregate to affect program integrity and form a basis for debarment even if individual violations seemed minor.

rubrics_metrics.name: Gross negligence and due diligence
rubrics_metrics.description: Gross negligence can be sufficient to support suspension or debarment; exercise of reasonable due diligence generally suffices to avoid a finding of simple negligence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Commission rejects proposals requiring recklessness as the minimum. A company that made good faith efforts to comply, even if submissions 'could result in overpayments', generally would not meet a 'grossly negligent' standard.

rubrics_metrics.name: Habitual non-payment of fees as cause
rubrics_metrics.description: Habitual non-payment or under-payment of Commission regulatory fees or required contributions may be a cause for suspension or debarment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: While the Guidelines separately permit action for uncontested debts, habitual nonpayment may also be viewed as repeated violations of Commission rules and assessed on the facts of each case.

rubrics_metrics.name: Aggravating and mitigating factors (adoption and expansion)
rubrics_metrics.description: The SDO should consider the aggravating and mitigating factors in 2 CFR 180.860 in both debarment and suspension proceedings; the Commission adopts these and adds allowable supplemental mitigating factors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: SDOs may consider additional mitigating factors such as remedies implemented after misconduct (likely to prevent recurrence) and whether proceedings to address alleged misconduct are pending before the Commission. Self-corrective actions can mitigate risk but will not create safe harbors.

rubrics_metrics.name: No creation of safe harbors for self-reporting or specific violations
rubrics_metrics.description: The Commission declines to create safe harbors for program violations or a statutory rule protecting self-reporting entities from suspension for a fixed period.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Although self-reporting and codes of conduct may be mitigating, the Commission retains discretion to pursue exclusion where appropriate despite such measures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consideration of impact on customers/end-users
rubrics_metrics.description: During suspension and debarment proceedings, the Commission should consider the impact that debarment would have on the provision of services to customers and end-users.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Impact is a factor to inform whether and under what terms to permit continuation or transition, but it is not a basis to allow a party to avoid suspension or debarment when misconduct otherwise warrants exclusion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evidentiary standards: adequate evidence for suspension; preponderance for debarment
rubrics_metrics.description: The Guidelines' evidentiary standards are adopted: 'adequate evidence' (information sufficient to support the reasonable belief that an act/omission occurred) for suspension and 'preponderance of the evidence' for debarment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The SDO must independently assess whether 'adequate evidence' exists to justify temporary suspension; unsubstantiated third-party assertions likely will not satisfy the standard. The procedural protections (notice, opportunity to respond) mitigate risk of erroneous suspension.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limitations on using issuance of Notices of Apparent Liability (NALs)
rubrics_metrics.description: Section 504(c) precludes using the fact of issuance of an NAL 'to the prejudice' of a person in other Commission proceedings, but does not prohibit using the underlying facts that support an NAL.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An SDO may rely on facts underpinning an NAL if those facts satisfy evidentiary standards, but may not treat issuance of the NAL itself as dispositive. Parties may submit evidence disputing the underlying facts in SDO proceedings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of program administrator findings and audits
rubrics_metrics.description: Findings by program administrators (e.g., USAC audits or commitment adjustments) may serve as causes if the underlying findings meet the Guidelines' evidentiary standards.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An SDO may consider such findings even if appeal of the administrator's decision is pending, but must independently evaluate the record. If the participant contests the exclusion, the SDO must render a final decision based on independent review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Respondent's ability to challenge facts in suspension proceedings
rubrics_metrics.description: In suspension proceedings, respondents may not challenge facts if the suspension is based on an indictment, conviction, civil judgment, or other findings by a body for which an opportunity to contest facts was provided, subject to exceptions where the underlying order has been modified or vacated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Commission adopts section 180.735(a)(1) with modification permitting respondents to bring to the SDO's attention information showing the original findings are no longer accurate (e.g., reconsideration, reversal, vacatur).

rubrics_metrics.name: Collateral estoppel application in debarment challenges
rubrics_metrics.description: For debarment proceedings, the SDO, in consultation with OGC, shall apply principles of collateral estoppel to determine whether a respondent may challenge findings set forth in Commission or other governmental orders for which an opportunity to contest the facts was provided.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This recognizes that Commission-level decisions and other judicial or administrative orders may be final for purposes of limiting re-litigation of facts in exclusion proceedings; contested facts in pending reconsideration or review may require referral to the full Commission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Delegation of exception-granting authority to the SDO
rubrics_metrics.description: The SDO is delegated initial authority to determine whether to grant an 'exception' permitting an excluded person to participate in a particular covered transaction (consistent with section 180.135 of the Guidelines and Supplemental Rule 6001.125), with review available by AFR/reconsideration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The proponent of an exception bears the burden of proving, by a preponderance of the evidence, any facts asserted to justify the exception. The SDO's decisions remain subject to AFR procedures and Commission oversight.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conditions on exceptions to exclusion
rubrics_metrics.description: Exceptions, if granted, shall be subject to appropriate conditions such as mandatory audits, additional reporting requirements, compliance agreements (with OGC approval), monitoring, or other effective oversight.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These conditions are intended to protect program integrity while permitting limited participation where necessary to ensure service continuity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Delegation of transition and continuation determinations to the SDO
rubrics_metrics.description: The SDO is responsible for determining appropriate transition and continuation periods before issuing any suspension or debarment order, and whether exceptions for extended continuation are appropriate to ensure delivery of services.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The SDO should evaluate sole source claims, consult program bureaus, and set terms/conditions for permitted continuations. The availability of alternate service providers is a relevant consideration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Presumption to require beneficiaries to transition away from excluded providers
rubrics_metrics.description: For the programs covered (e.g., Lifeline, E-Rate, RHC), the Commission presumes the SDO will require beneficiaries receiving services from an excluded provider to transition to new providers, rather than allowing continuations under section 180.310/180.315 of the Guidelines.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This presumption is based on program experience: resellers typically have underlying carriers available; beneficiaries can transition to other providers. Transition periods should be sufficient for any necessary rebidding or procurement activities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treatment of resellers and principals during exclusions
rubrics_metrics.description: Where exclusions involve resellers, alternative providers usually exist (e.g., underlying carriers); principals such as officers or program managers internal to organizations must be removed and their duties transferred to other individuals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: SDOs should ensure organizations replace excluded individuals in covered transactions and that beneficiaries have opportunity and time to transition to alternate providers as appropriate.
